alta-badia.character: Sella, Gardena, Pordoi, Campolongo, Fedaia, Giau and Valparola around the Sella massif – the densest pass country in the Alps, busy in summer.
alta-badia.multiDay: A week without repeating a road; the Sellaronda in half a day, the Maratona loop a day.
alta-badia.access: Bressanone or Brunico railway station, then bus; Bolzano and Innsbruck in an hour and a half.

andermatt.character: Furka, Grimsel, Susten, Gotthard with the Tremola, Oberalp and Nufenen from one crossroads: nowhere else are so many high passes so close together.
andermatt.multiDay: Four days for the classic loops; the three-pass loop in a day.
andermatt.access: Andermatt railway station (Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn) via Göschenen; Zurich in two hours.

andorra-cerdanya.character: The high passes of the eastern Pyrenees: the Envalira, Ordino and Arcalís in Andorra, the Puymorens and Pailhères on the French side, plus the Toses and Cantó in Catalonia. Sunnier and drier than the west.
andorra-cerdanya.multiDay: A week based in Andorra with a second base in Ax-les-Thermes.
andorra-cerdanya.access: Ax-les-Thermes by train from Toulouse, Andorra by bus from Toulouse or Barcelona.

aostatal.character: Great and Little St Bernard, San Carlo and the quiet side valleys of Valsavarenche and Valgrisenche beneath the Gran Paradiso.
aostatal.multiDay: Four to five days; the two St Bernard passes link to France and Switzerland.
aostatal.access: Aosta railway station via Turin; A5 motorway from Turin.

ariege.character: The wild passes of the Couserans and the Vicdessos: the Agnes, Lers, Core, Port and Latrape, plus the Plateau de Beille. Hardly any traffic, many pastures.
ariege.multiDay: Three to four days from Saint-Girons or Massat.
ariege.access: Toulouse by train to Foix, then an hour into the Couserans.

baskenland.character: The green passes of the French Basque country: the Bagargui with the Iraty pastures and the small Ispéguy across the border. Mild, damp and rideable early in the year.
baskenland.multiDay: Two to three days from Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port, a good start to a Pyrenees crossing.

bayerisches-oberland.character: The Wallberg, the Spitzingsattel, the Sudelfeld and the Kesselberg: short, steep climbs between foothill lakes, an hour from Munich.
bayerisches-oberland.multiDay: A long weekend; over the Achenpass into the Inn valley and on into Tyrol.
bayerisches-oberland.access: Bayerische Regiobahn from Munich to Tegernsee and Schliersee.

bearn-ossau.character: The western Pyrenees between the Ossau and the Barétous: the Aubisque, Marie-Blanque, Pourtalet, Somport and the Pierre Saint-Martin. Greener and quieter than the Hautes-Pyrénées.
bearn-ossau.multiDay: Three to four days from Laruns, with trips across the border into Aragon.
bearn-ossau.access: Pau by TGV or plane, then an hour into the Ossau.

belluneser-dolomiten.character: Duran, Cereda, Croce d'Aune and the two Forcelle around the national park between Agordo and Feltre, plus Rolle, Valles, Brocon and San Boldo at the edge: the quiet southern side of the Dolomites, lower and emptier than the Sella and Cortina.
belluneser-dolomiten.multiDay: Four to five days; the loop over Cereda, Rolle and Valles in a day, Duran and Staulanza on a second, the Grappa as a day trip from Feltre.
belluneser-dolomiten.access: Feltre railway station on the Padua–Belluno line, bus to Agordo from Belluno; Venice or Treviso airport a good hour away.

berchtesgaden-salzkammergut.character: Rossfeld, Postalm and Loser: managed panoramic roads on the northern edge of the Alps, open early in the year and with views out across the foothills.
berchtesgaden-salzkammergut.multiDay: Three days; the Grossglockner High Alpine Road is a day's stage away.
berchtesgaden-salzkammergut.access: Berchtesgaden or Bad Ischl railway station; Salzburg with airport in half an hour.

bergamasker-alpen.character: San Marco, Vivione, Aprica, Selvino and Colle Gallo: the forgotten passes between Bergamo and the Valtellina, steep, quiet and at home in the Giro.
bergamasker-alpen.multiDay: Four days; Mortirolo and Gavia lie at the eastern end of the Valtellina.
bergamasker-alpen.access: Morbegno or Bergamo railway station; Bergamo airport in an hour.

berner-jura.character: The Jura ridge above the Three Lakes region: the Chasseral, Vue des Alpes and Mont-Crosin, plus the steep Weissenstein above Solothurn. Pastures, forest and in clear weather the whole Alpine chain.
berner-jura.multiDay: Two to three days between Saint-Imier and Solothurn, a good weekend from Basel, Bern or Zurich.
berner-jura.access: Saint-Imier and Solothurn by train, an hour from Bern or Basel.

bormio-livigno.character: Stelvio, Gavia, Mortirolo, Umbrail and the passes around Livigno: the highest roads in Italy packed into the smallest space.
bormio-livigno.multiDay: Five days; the Stelvio–Umbrail loop and Gavia–Mortirolo a day each, the rest for Foscagno and Eira.
bormio-livigno.access: No railway station; Tirano (Bernina railway) with a bus, Milan in three hours.

brianconnais-queyras.character: Izoard, Granon, Agnel, Montgenèvre and the gorges of the Guil: high, dry, sunny – Briançon itself sits at 1,300 m.
brianconnais-queyras.multiDay: A week with two bases; into Italy over the Agnel or Montgenèvre, south over Vars into the Ubaye.
brianconnais-queyras.access: Briançon railway station (night train from Paris); Turin via the Fréjus tunnel or Montgenèvre.

bugey.character: The southern Jura between the Rhône and the Valromey: the Grand Colombier with four sides, plus the Biche, Richemond and the Mont du Chat above the Lac du Bourget. Steep, wooded and quiet.
bugey.multiDay: Three to four days from Culoz, rideable earlier and later in the year than the high Alps next door.
bugey.access: Culoz by train via Geneva, Lyon or Chambéry.

champsaur.character: The quiet high valley north of Gap: the Noyer as the one big name, plus the Manse, Chaillol and Orcières, sunnier than the Écrins behind it.
champsaur.multiDay: Two to three days from Gap, as a stage between the Oisans and the Ubaye.
champsaur.access: Gap by train from Grenoble or Marseille.

chartreuse-bauges.character: Two limestone massifs either side of Chambéry: short passes below cliffs, a lot of forest and little traffic, mid-height rather than high alpine.
chartreuse-bauges.multiDay: Three to four days of loops from Chambéry, rideable early in the year and late in autumn when the high passes are closed.
chartreuse-bauges.access: Chambéry by TGV from Paris or via Lyon, the passes start at the edge of town.

churer-rheintal-liechtenstein.character: Malbun, the Lenzerheide, Arosa and Flumserberg: steep climbs straight out of the low Rhine valley, each a dead end or a crossing of its own, with flat paths along the Rhine in between.
churer-rheintal-liechtenstein.multiDay: Three to four days with short approaches; the Lenzerheide leads on to the Albula and the Julier into the Engadine, the Furkajoch into Vorarlberg.
churer-rheintal-liechtenstein.access: Chur, Landquart and Sargans stations on the line from Zurich (just over an hour); Vaduz by bus from Sargans, Buchs or Feldkirch.

comer-see.character: Ghisallo, Muro di Sormano, San Primo, Valcava and the Culmine: the climbs of Il Lombardia, rideable all year round, full of road bikes on Sundays.
comer-see.multiDay: Four days in spring or autumn; Ticino and the Bergamo Alps are a day's loop away.
comer-see.access: Lecco or Como railway station; Milan with airport in an hour.

cortina.character: Tre Cime, Giau, Falzarego, Tre Croci, Staulanza and Duran: the eastern Dolomites, quieter than the Sella area and with the most famous dead-end finish in the Alps.
cortina.multiDay: Five days; to Alta Badia over the Falzarego as a stage.
cortina.access: Calalzo or Dobbiaco railway station, then bus; Venice in two hours.

cuneo.character: Fauniera, Sampeyre, Agnello, Lombarde and the Maira valley: the loneliest high roads in the Alps, from a town with a railway station.
cuneo.multiDay: A week without repeating a road; over the Lombarde into France as a stage.
cuneo.access: Cuneo railway station via Turin; Turin airport in an hour and a half.

engadin.character: Albula, Julier, Bernina, Flüela, Maloja and Ofen around a high valley at 1,800 m – the climbs start high and the air is thin.
engadin.multiDay: A week; to Livigno and into the Val Müstair over the Ofen pass as stages.
engadin.access: St. Moritz railway station via Chur (Rhaetian Railway); Zurich in three hours.

ennstal-dachstein.character: The Stoderzinken, the Radstädter Tauern, the Sölkpass and the Postalm: viewpoint roads and Tauern crossings around the Enns valley, with the Dachstein behind.
ennstal-dachstein.multiDay: Four to five days; the Sölkpass links to the Mur valley, the Radstädter Tauern to the Lungau.
ennstal-dachstein.access: Schladming station on the Enns valley line; Salzburg in just over an hour.

fassa-fiemme.character: Rolle, Valles, San Pellegrino, Manghen, Lavazè and Costalunga: the southern Dolomite passes, wooded and less busy than the Sella massif.
fassa-fiemme.multiDay: Five days; the Sella passes are a day's loop away.
fassa-fiemme.access: Trento or Bolzano railway station, then bus into the Val di Fiemme.

gardasee.character: Strada della Forra, Ballino, Punta Veleno and the heights above the lake: short, steep climbs with the water at your back, from March to November.
gardasee.multiDay: A week in spring or autumn; Monte Bondone and the Brenta passes are a day's loop away.
gardasee.access: Rovereto railway station (Brenner line); Verona with airport in an hour.

haute-savoie.character: Aravis, Colombière, Romme, Joux-Plane and Ramaz – the mid-height passes of the Tour de France between Annecy and Lake Geneva, green, closely packed and open early in the year.
haute-savoie.multiDay: A week without repeating a road; the Route des Grandes Alpes starts here and leads over Roselend into the Tarentaise.
haute-savoie.access: Geneva airport in an hour; Annecy, Cluses or Thonon railway station.

hautes-pyrenees.character: The heart of the Tour's Pyrenees: the Tourmalet, Aspin, Hautacam, Luz Ardiden and the Portet, plus quiet passes like the Spandelles and the Hourquette. Long, steep climbs of over 1,000 m.
hautes-pyrenees.multiDay: A week based in Argelès or Luz with a second base in Saint-Lary; the Cercle de la Mort over the Aubisque, Tourmalet, Aspin and Peyresourde as the queen stage.
hautes-pyrenees.access: Lourdes by TGV, Tarbes-Lourdes or Pau by plane.

hochjura-vallee-de-joux.character: The Jura ridge above Lake Geneva: the Faucille, Givrine, Marchairuz and Mollendruz, pastures, lakes and forest at the top, the view of the Alps below.
hochjura-vallee-de-joux.multiDay: Two to three days, as a loop around the Vallée de Joux and across the border to Les Rousses.
hochjura-vallee-de-joux.access: Nyon or Geneva by train, the passes start at the lakeshore.

hochvogesen.character: The Schlucht, the Route des Crêtes and the Hohneck above the Munster valley: grassy crests at 1200 to 1350 m, short steep climbs out of the valleys, and motorbikes on the crest at weekends.
hochvogesen.multiDay: A base for a long weekend up to four days; the loop over the Schlucht, the crest road and the Grand Ballon in a day, the south with the Ballon d'Alsace one stage away.
hochvogesen.access: By train to Colmar and on by regional train to Munster; the nearest airports are Basel-Mulhouse and Strasbourg.

hohe-tauern.character: The Grossglockner High Alpine Road, Sportgastein, Kals and the Kitzbüheler Horn: managed toll roads, high and well kept, plus the steepest dead-end climb in Austria.
hohe-tauern.multiDay: Three to four days; the Glockner into Carinthia as a stage.
hohe-tauern.access: Zell am See or Kitzbühel railway station; Salzburg in an hour and a half.

innsbruck-wipptal.character: Jaufen, Penser Joch and Kühtai on either side of the Brenner – long, steady climbs from two towns with railway stations.
innsbruck-wipptal.multiDay: Four days; over the Timmelsjoch into the Ötztal or over the Jaufen into the Passeier valley as stages.
innsbruck-wipptal.access: Innsbruck or Sterzing railway station on the Brenner line; Innsbruck airport.

julische-alpen.character: Vršič with its cobbled hairpins, Predil, Mangart as a dead-end road, Wurzen and Loibl: the three-country corner of Slovenia, Italy and Austria.
julische-alpen.multiDay: Four days; the Vršič–Predil loop a day, the Soča valley a second.
julische-alpen.access: Jesenice railway station; Ljubljana with airport in an hour.

karnische-alpen.character: Zoncolan, Plöcken, Nassfeld, Sella Nevea and Monte Croce Comelico – the steepest mountain of the Giro and the quiet border passes into Carinthia.
karnische-alpen.multiDay: Four days; the Julian Alps and Cortina as stage destinations.
karnische-alpen.access: Carnia railway station (Udine–Tarvisio), then bus to Tolmezzo; Venice in two hours.

ligurien.character: Poggio, Cipressa and the hinterland of Sanremo: low passes, rideable all year round, in winter the training camp of the pros.
ligurien.multiDay: A week in the winter half of the year; in summer avoid the coast and head early into the hinterland.
ligurien.access: Sanremo and Imperia railway stations on the coastal line; Nice airport in an hour.

luchon-aran.character: Around Luchon: the Peyresourde, Superbagnères, Balès, Menté and Portet d'Aspet, plus the Val d'Aran and the Bonaigua over the Portillon.
luchon-aran.multiDay: Four to five days from Luchon, with a detour into Spain.
luchon-aran.access: Toulouse by train or plane, then two hours to Luchon.

maurienne.character: The valley with the most climbs of the Tour: Madeleine, Croix de Fer, Glandon, Télégraphe, Mollard, Chaussy with the Lacets de Montvernier – all of them start on the valley floor.
maurienne.multiDay: A week without repeating a road; the Route des Grandes Alpes runs straight through it, and the Galibier links to Briançon.
maurienne.access: Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne railway station with a TGV stop; the A43 motorway runs through the valley.

mercantour.character: Turini, Braus, Castillon, Vence and the gorges of the Cians – from the sea into the mountains, and in winter the mildest road-cycling area in the Alps.
mercantour.multiDay: October to April the place for a week; in summer start early, the coast roads are hot and busy.
mercantour.access: Nice airport and railway station; the railway line into the Roya valley stops at Sospel.

monte-rosa.character: Breuil-Cervinia below the Matterhorn, the Col de Joux, the long Gressoney valley and Oropa above Biella: valley climbs from the floor of the Aosta valley to the foot of the four-thousanders, open to the top all year.
monte-rosa.multiDay: Three to four days; with Pila and Cogne in the upper Aosta valley a week, and the Great St Bernard leads on into the Valais.
monte-rosa.access: Châtillon-Saint-Vincent station on the Turin–Aosta line; Turin and Milan in an hour and a half to two hours.

nockberge.character: Nockalmstrasse, Turracher Höhe, Malta High Alpine Road and the Villacher Alpenstrasse: gentle alpine-pasture heights and long toll roads, little traffic, lots of views.
nockberge.multiDay: Three to four days; into Slovenia over the Wurzen or Loibl as a stage.
nockberge.access: Villach or Spittal railway station; Klagenfurt with airport.

oetztal.character: Timmelsjoch, Kühtai, the Ötztal and Kaunertal glacier roads, Pitztal: the climbs of the Ötztaler Radmarathon and the glacier roads as dead ends.
oetztal.multiDay: Four to five days; the marathon loop in a day, the Timmelsjoch into South Tyrol as a stage.
oetztal.access: Ötztal railway station on the Arlberg line; Innsbruck in an hour.

oisans.character: Alpe d'Huez, Galibier, Croix de Fer and Sarenne in one spot: big altitudes, big names, and plenty of traffic on the D1091 through the Romanche gorge.
oisans.multiDay: A base for four to six days; the Marmotte loop in a day, and a stage over the Galibier to Briançon is possible.
oisans.access: Grenoble by rail, Lyon airport in an hour and a half; the bus into the valley runs as far as Bourg-d'Oisans.

ossola.character: The south side of the Simplon, Macugnaga below the east face of the Monte Rosa and the Val Formazza up to the Toce waterfall: long, moderately steep valleys from a low, warm valley floor.
ossola.multiDay: Three days; the Simplon links to the Valais, and Lake Maggiore with the Mottarone lies half an hour to the south.
ossola.access: Domodossola station on the Simplon line, direct from Brig, Geneva, Bern and Milan.

osttirol.character: Gailbergsattel and Kartitscher Sattel, the Staller Sattel into the Defereggental, Kals and, over the Iselsberg, the Grossglockner road: Lienz lies where the Drau, Isel and Puster valleys meet, and almost every climb starts only after a ride along the valley.
osttirol.multiDay: Three to four days; the Dolomitenradrundfahrt loop in a day, a stage to Cortina or into the Gailtal.
osttirol.access: Lienz railway station with trains from Villach and through the Pustertal from Innsbruck; Klagenfurt airport a good two hours by train.

simmental-saanenland.character: The Jaunpass, the Col du Pillon, the Col des Mosses and the Gurnigel, plus Adelboden and the Iffigenalp: green prealpine passes between the Bernese Oberland and the Vaud Alps.
simmental-saanenland.multiDay: Four days; over the Col du Pillon and the Col de la Croix into the Rhône valley and on into the Valais.
simmental-saanenland.access: Zweisimmen station on the Spiez–Montreux line; Bern in just over an hour.

steiermark.character: The Gaberl, the Weinebene, the Klippitztörl and the Schöckl: long, steady alpine passes instead of rock, green and quiet, with the Erzberg at the Präbichl as the odd one out.
steiermark.multiDay: Three to four days from Graz; rideable early and late in the year while the Tauern are still closed.
steiermark.access: Graz main station, Graz airport; Vienna in two and a half hours.

suedvogesen.character: The Ballon d'Alsace, La Planche des Belles Filles and the Grand Ballon – the Tour de France climbs of the Vosges – with quiet wooded passes between them and the busy N66 over Bussang.
suedvogesen.multiDay: Two to three days; the loop over the Hundsruck, the Ballon d'Alsace and Bussang in a day, the Planche as a detour from Plancher-les-Mines.
suedvogesen.access: By TGV to Mulhouse and on by train to Thann and up the Thur valley; for the west side Belfort-Montbéliard TGV.

susa-piemont.character: Finestre with its gravel, Sestriere, Mont Cenis and the Nivolet – the Piedmont side of the Western Alps, Giro country.
susa-piemont.multiDay: Four days; over Montgenèvre or Mont Cenis into France as a stage.
susa-piemont.access: Susa railway station via Turin; Turin in an hour.

tarentaise.character: Iseran, Petit Saint-Bernard, Cormet de Roselend and the ski resorts as dead-end roads – high, long climbs, open late in the year.
tarentaise.multiDay: Four to five days; the Iseran to Bonneval and the Petit Saint-Bernard to Aosta are stages, not loops.
tarentaise.access: Bourg-Saint-Maurice railway station, TGV in winter, otherwise via Chambéry.

tessin.character: Monte Ceneri, Alpe di Neggia, Generoso, Bisbino and the valley roads of the Verzasca and Bavona: lakes, palms and steep little roads, from March to November.
tessin.multiDay: Five days in spring or autumn; the Nufenen into Valais and the Lukmanier into Graubünden as stages.
tessin.access: Locarno, Lugano or Stresa railway station on the Gotthard and Simplon lines; Milan with airport in an hour and a half.

trentino-brenta.character: Monte Bondone, Campo Carlo Magno, Tonale, Mendel and the car-free Val di Genova around the Brenta Dolomites – Giro country without the crowds of the Sella massif.
trentino-brenta.multiDay: Five days; Lake Garda to the south and the Stelvio to the north-west are stage destinations.
trentino-brenta.access: Trento or Rovereto railway station (Brenner line); Verona with airport in an hour.

ubaye.character: Bonette, Vars, Allos, Cayolle and Pra-Loup from a quiet valley – the highest roads in the Alps with the least traffic.
ubaye.multiDay: Five days are not enough; the Bonette alone is a day, and the loop over Allos and Cayolle a second.
ubaye.access: No railway station; Gap or Digne by rail, then bus. By car via Gap or from Cuneo over the Col de Larche.

venetische-voralpen.character: Cima Grappa with its ten ascents, the Asiago plateau, Vezzena, Fugazze and San Boldo: the southern edge of the Alps, rideable from February to December.
venetische-voralpen.multiDay: Five days in spring or autumn; the southern Dolomites are a day's loop away.
venetische-voralpen.access: Bassano del Grappa railway station; Venice and Verona with airports in an hour.

ventoux.character: One mountain with three ascents and, all around, the small passes of the Baronnies and the Gorges de la Nesque: lavender, limestone, mistral.
ventoux.multiDay: Three days for the three sides of the Ventoux, the rest for the Baronnies; in high summer the mountain is hot and busy.
ventoux.access: Avignon TGV, then an hour by car; Orange via the A7 motorway.

vercors.character: Combe Laval, the Gorges de la Bourne and the Rousset: balcony roads carved into the cliff face instead of passes, and a quiet plateau on top.
vercors.multiDay: Three to four days of balcony roads and plateau; to Grenoble or Die as a stage.
vercors.access: Grenoble or Valence by TGV, then an hour up to the plateau.

vinschgau.character: The Stelvio from the north side, the Martell, Ulten and Schnals valleys as quiet dead ends beneath glaciers, and the Reschen to warm up.
vinschgau.multiDay: Four days; over the Stelvio to Bormio as a stage.
vinschgau.access: Vinschgau railway from Merano to Mals; Bolzano with rail and airport.

vorarlberg-allgaeu.character: Furkajoch, Faschinajoch, Hochtannberg, Arlberg, Riedberg and the Silvretta High Alpine Road: the northern edge of the Alps between the Bregenzerwald and the Allgäu, green and with long climbs.
vorarlberg-allgaeu.multiDay: Four days; the Silvretta and the Arlberg link into the Tyrolean Oberland.
vorarlberg-allgaeu.access: Bludenz, Langen am Arlberg or Oberstdorf railway station; Zurich and Munich in two hours.

wallis.character: Grand-Saint-Bernard, Forclaz, Sanetsch, Simplon and Nufenen from the deep Rhône valley – long climbs, a dry climate, the valley itself warm.
wallis.multiDay: A week with two bases; the Simplon into Italy and the Nufenen into Ticino as stages.
wallis.access: Martigny and Brig railway stations on the Simplon line; Geneva in an hour and a half.

zentralschweiz.character: Klausen, Pragel, Glaubenbielen, Glaubenberg and the car-free Grosse Scheidegg – the pre-alpine passes between Lake Lucerne and Lake Brienz, shorter than the Gotthard giants and open earlier in the year.
zentralschweiz.multiDay: Four days; Susten and Grimsel as the link southwards.
zentralschweiz.access: Meiringen, Lucerne or Altdorf railway station; Zurich in an hour.

zillertal.character: The Zillertaler Höhenstraße, Hintertux and the Gerlospass: steep ramps out of a deep, wide valley, the Höhenstraße one of the hardest in Austria.
zillertal.multiDay: Three days; the Gerlospass leads to the Krimml waterfalls and on into the Hohe Tauern.
zillertal.access: The Zillertal railway from Jenbach to Mayrhofen; Innsbruck in an hour.

westerzgebirge.character: The two highest mountains of the Ore Mountains on either side of the border, plus the long climbs out of the Ohře valley: plateaus at 900 to 1200 m, spruce forest and wide meadows, little traffic away from the main road.
westerzgebirge.multiDay: A long weekend: the Fichtelberg and the Klínovec in one day, Měděnec or the Auersberg on the second.
westerzgebirge.access: By train to Cranzahl and on with the Fichtelberg narrow-gauge railway to Oberwiesenthal; a good hour by car from Chemnitz, two from Prague.

osterzgebirge.character: The Ore Mountains' steep escarpment towards Bohemia: short, steep climbs out of Krupka, Dubí and Osek onto a gentle ridge, with quiet roads at the top between Altenberg and Moldava.
osterzgebirge.multiDay: Two days are enough for every climb on the Bohemian side; from Altenberg as loops over the border, from Teplice from below.
osterzgebirge.access: By train from Dresden via Heidenau to Altenberg, or to Teplice via Ústí nad Labem; Dresden is an hour away.

suedschwarzwald.character: The highest mountains of the Black Forest between Freiburg and the Feldberg: long climbs of 500 to 900 metres out of the Rhine plain and the valleys, forest and open pastures at the top, traffic on the main roads.
suedschwarzwald.multiDay: A base for a long weekend up to a week: the Schauinsland, the Notschrei and the Feldberg make one loop, the Kandel, the Wiedener Eck and the Blauen another day each.
suedschwarzwald.access: By ICE to Freiburg, from there on the Höllental railway into the Dreisam valley; Basel-Mulhouse airport is an hour away.

nordschwarzwald.character: The national park around the Black Forest High Road: climbs out of the valleys on the Rhine side onto a long ridge at 900 to 1000 m, moorland and distant views at the top, quiet valleys below.
nordschwarzwald.multiDay: A weekend: the Ruhestein and the Kniebis as a loop over the high road, the valleys on the Rhine side as a second day.
nordschwarzwald.access: By train to Baiersbronn or Freudenstadt; a good hour from Karlsruhe and Stuttgart.

serra-de-tramuntana.character: The range on Mallorca's north-west coast: Sa Calobra, the Puig Major and the Coll de Sóller above the sea, limestone, olive groves and hairpins, from sea level to nearly 900 m. Full of cycling groups in spring, hot in high summer.
serra-de-tramuntana.multiDay: A week, the way most riders do it: Sa Calobra, the loop over Puig Major and the Coll de Sóller, Lluc from both sides, and on a rainy day Randa or Sant Salvador on the plain.
serra-de-tramuntana.access: Palma airport, from there an hour to Port de Pollença or half an hour to Sóller; every major airline carries bikes.

monts-du-cantal.character: Europe's largest extinct volcano, a circle of green valleys around the Puy Mary: the Pas de Peyrol, the Néronne and Prat de Bouc, pastures, burons and hardly any traffic. Wait for June and September; muggy in high summer, closed at the top in winter.
monts-du-cantal.multiDay: Three days are enough: the Pas de Peyrol from two sides, the loop over the Néronne from Salers and Prat de Bouc from Murat.
monts-du-cantal.access: Train to Murat (via Clermont-Ferrand), by car the A75; nearest airports Aurillac or Clermont-Ferrand.

monts-dore.character: The volcanoes around the Puy de Sancy, the highest mountain of the Massif Central: the Croix Saint-Robert, the Croix-Morand and the Tour finish at Super-Besse close together, with crater lakes. Good for a long weekend.
monts-dore.multiDay: Two days: the loop over the Croix Saint-Robert and Super-Besse, and the Croix-Morand with the Lac Chambon.
monts-dore.access: By car via Clermont-Ferrand (one hour); train to Le Mont-Dore in summer only.

cevennen.character: Chestnut woods, deep valleys and bare granite ridges between the Mont Lozère and the Aigoual: long steady climbs and empty roads, with a Mediterranean climate in the south. Spring and autumn; hot in the valleys in high summer.
cevennen.multiDay: Four days: the Aigoual from Valleraugue and from Meyrueis, the Minier from Le Vigan, the Mont Lozère over the Finiels; the Gorges du Tarn in between.
cevennen.access: By car via the A75 or from Nîmes; nearest stations Alès or Mende.

harz.character: The northernmost low range with real climbs: the car-free Brocken, Torfhaus above Bad Harzburg and the short steep ramps above the Bode gorge. Spruce forest, moors and half-timbered towns around the edge, for a weekend from Berlin, Hamburg or Hanover.
harz.multiDay: Two days: the Brocken and Torfhaus from Wernigerode or Bad Harzburg, the Hexentanzplatz and the Rosstrappe in a morning at Thale.
harz.access: Train to Wernigerode, Bad Harzburg or Thale; by car via the A7 or the B6.

thueringer-wald.character: The ridge of the Rennsteig: spruce forest, winter sports resorts and two named climbs, the Inselsberg and Oberhof. More low range than mountains, for a weekend.
thueringer-wald.multiDay: A weekend: the Inselsberg from both sides and Oberhof, with a stretch of the Rennsteig between them.
thueringer-wald.access: Train to Oberhof or Gotha, by car via the A71 or the A4.

rhoen.character: The land of open views: bare plateaus, gliders over the Wasserkuppe and the monastery beer at the Kreuzberg. Short climbs, a lot of wind, little traffic during the week.
rhoen.multiDay: Two days: the Wasserkuppe from two sides, the Kreuzberg and the Hochrhön road as a loop.
rhoen.access: Train to Fulda or Bad Neustadt, by car via the A7.

arberland.character: The two roads over the Arber, the Bretterschachten and the Brennes, on one loop from Bodenmais or Bayerisch Eisenstein. Spruce forest, a cable car and the Arbersee; the Bohemian Forest just across the border.
arberland.multiDay: A weekend: the loop around the Arber over both passes, plus a day into the Bohemian Forest via Železná Ruda and Špičák.
arberland.access: Train to Bayerisch Eisenstein or Bodenmais, by car via the A3 and Deggendorf.

boehmerwald.character: The Czech side of the border range: the Kleť above Český Krumlov, the Churáňov above Stachy and the Dreisessel on the Bavarian border. Long, even climbs through spruce forest, quiet roads and the Vltava in the valley.
boehmerwald.multiDay: Three days from Český Krumlov: the Kleť in the morning, the Churáňov as a long loop via Vimperk, the Dreisessel via the Lipno reservoir.
boehmerwald.access: Train to Český Krumlov via České Budějovice; by car from Passau or Linz.

alta-rocca.character: The south of Corsica between granite needles and the sea: the Col de Bavella above Zonza and the long climb to the Ospedale above Porto-Vecchio. Pine forest, bathing pools and beaches on the same day.
alta-rocca.multiDay: Three days: the Ospedale and Zonza as a loop from Porto-Vecchio, Bavella from both sides, a day on the coast.
alta-rocca.access: Ferry or flight to Figari or Bastia, by car along the east coast.

zentralkorsika.character: The middle of the island around Vivario: Vizzavona, Sorba and Verde in deep pine and beech forests, quiet roads apart from the trunk road. Corte, with its station, as the base.
zentralkorsika.multiDay: Three days from Corte: Vizzavona and Sorba as a loop via Vivario and Ghisoni, the Verde as a long day, plus the Restonica gorge.
zentralkorsika.access: Train to Corte from Bastia or Ajaccio; by car on the T20.

westkorsika.character: The mountains above the Gulf of Porto: the Col de Vergio, the highest road pass on the island, and the Col de Sevi above Vico. Laricio pines, the Spelunca gorges and the sea in sight.
westkorsika.multiDay: Two days from Evisa: the Vergio in the morning, the Sevi via Vico as a loop; plus the Calanche de Piana on the coast.
westkorsika.access: By car from Ajaccio via Sagone or from Porto; no station nearby.

teneriffa.character: The island around the Teide: four ways into the Cañadas, each over 1,500 metres, plus the Masca hairpins. The pros' training camp in winter, often cloudy in the north, sunny in the south.
teneriffa.multiDay: A week: the Teide from the north and from the west, Izaña along the ridge, Masca, and a rest day by the sea.
teneriffa.access: Fly to Tenerife South or North, bring the bike or hire one there.

gran-canaria.character: A round island with its highest point in the middle: uphill from every coast, through gorges and pine forest to the Pico de las Nieves and the Cruz de Tejeda. Sunny in the south, cool at the top.
gran-canaria.multiDay: Five days from Maspalomas: Fataga, the Pico de las Nieves, the Cruz de Tejeda via Ayacata, the west coast via Mogán.
gran-canaria.access: Fly to Gran Canaria, transfer to the southern resorts; bike hire in Maspalomas.

la-palma.character: The green island in the west: the Roque de los Muchachos, 2,400 metres from the sea, plus steep roads through laurel forest and hardly any traffic. For climbers who want peace.
la-palma.multiDay: Three days: the Roque from Santa Cruz, the northern loop via Barlovento and Garafía, the volcanoes in the south.
la-palma.access: Fly to La Palma or take the ferry from Tenerife.

zentralasturien.character: The Vuelta mountains south of Oviedo: the Angliru, the Cobertoria, the San Lorenzo, the Farrapona and the Pajares in green valleys, steep, narrow and empty. Atlantic weather, pleasantly cool in summer.
zentralasturien.multiDay: Five days: the Angliru, the Cobertoria and the Pajares from Pola de Lena, the San Lorenzo and the Farrapona from Somiedo.
zentralasturien.access: Fly to Asturias (Oviedo), train to Pola de Lena; by car on the AP-66.

picos-de-europa.character: Limestone mountains between Asturias, Cantabria and León: the Lagos de Covadonga, the Vuelta's most famous finish, and the San Glorio with the view over the whole massif. Deep gorges in between.
picos-de-europa.multiDay: Four days: Covadonga from Cangas de Onís, the Hermida gorge to Potes, the San Glorio and Fuente Dé.
picos-de-europa.access: Fly to Asturias or Santander, by car on the A-8.

sierra-nevada.character: The mountains above Granada: Spain's highest road up to almost 2,500 m, the Purche and the hard Hazallanas ramp. Ridden from the city, in summer only early in the morning.
sierra-nevada.multiDay: Three days from Granada: the Sierra Nevada up to the Hoya de la Mora, Hazallanas, the Purche with the Alhambra in the afternoon.
sierra-nevada.access: Fly to Granada or Málaga, train to Granada.

sierra-de-los-filabres.character: Bare mountains above the Tabernas desert: Calar Alto with its observatory and the Velefique hairpins, two Vuelta climbs without traffic. For spring and autumn, too hot in summer.
sierra-de-los-filabres.multiDay: Two days from Tabernas: Calar Alto via Gérgal, Velefique with the descent via Bacares.
sierra-de-los-filabres.access: Fly to Almería, by car on the A-92.

majella.character: The limestone massif above the Adriatic: the Blockhaus, the hardest Giro mountain of the south, and the Passo Lanciano through beech forest. An hour from the coast.
majella.multiDay: Two days: the Blockhaus from Roccamorice, the Passo Lanciano from Pretoro with the descent to Guardiagrele.
majella.access: Fly or take the train to Pescara, then drive into the mountains.

gran-sasso.character: The highest mountains of the Apennines between the Abruzzo and Lazio: Campo Imperatore across the plain below the Corno Grande and the Terminillo above Rieti. Long climbs, wide country.
gran-sasso.multiDay: Three days: Campo Imperatore from Fonte Cerreto, the Terminillo from Rieti, the Rocca di Mezzo plateau in between.
gran-sasso.access: Train to L'Aquila or Rieti, by car from Rome in an hour and a half.

appennino-tosco-emiliano.character: The green ridge between Tuscany and Emilia: the Abetone through fir forest and San Pellegrino in Alpe with its walls over 15 %. Cool in summer, quiet outside the holidays.
appennino-tosco-emiliano.multiDay: Three days from Abetone: the pass from both sides, San Pellegrino via the Garfagnana, the Foce delle Radici.
appennino-tosco-emiliano.access: By car via Pistoia or Modena; train to Pistoia.
